exam: 2021年6月 第3套 · 仔细阅读 P2
title: Can you remember what you ate yesterday?…

sents.en: Can you remember what you ate yesterday?
sents.cn: 你还记得昨天吃了什么吗？

sents.en: If asked, most people will be able to give a vague description of their main meals: breakfast, lunch, dinner.
sents.cn: 如果被问起，大多数人都能大致描述自己的主餐：早饭、午饭、晚饭。

sents.en: But can you be sure you've noted every snack bar in your car, or every handful of nuts at your desk?
sents.cn: 但你敢确定自己记下了车里的每一根能量棒，或办公桌上的每一把坚果吗？

sents.en: Most people will have a feeling that they've missed something out.
sents.cn: 大多数人大概都会觉得漏掉了什么。

sents.en: We originally had this suspicion back in 2016, puzzled by the fact that national statistics showed calorie consumption falling dramatically over past decades.
sents.cn: 我们最早在2016年就有了这种怀疑，当时我们困惑于一个事实：全国统计显示，过去几十年里卡路里摄入量急剧下降。

sents.en: We found reliable evidence that people were drastically under-reporting what they ate.
sents.cn: 我们找到了可靠证据，表明人们严重低报了自己的饮食。

sents.en: Now the Office for National Statistics has confirmed that we are consuming 50% more calories than our national statistics claim.
sents.cn: 如今，英国国家统计局已证实，我们的卡路里实际摄入量比全国统计所声称的高出50%。

sents.en: Why is this happening?
sents.cn: 为什么会这样？

sents.en: We can point to at least three potential causes.
sents.cn: 我们至少能指出三个潜在原因。

sents.en: One is the rise in obesity levels itself.
sents.cn: 其一是肥胖水平本身的上升。

sents.en: Under-reporting rates are much higher for obese people, because they simply consume more food, and thus have more to remember.
sents.cn: 肥胖者的低报率要高得多，因为他们摄入的食物更多，因而需要记住的也更多。

sents.en: Another cause is that the proportion of people who are trying to lose weight has been increasing over time.
sents.cn: 另一个原因是，随着时间推移，试图减肥的人群比例不断上升。

sents.en: People who want to lose weight are more likely to under-report their eating·regardless of whether they are overweight or not.
sents.cn: 想要减肥的人更可能低报自己的饮食——无论他们是否超重。

sents.en: This may be driven partly by self-deception or "wishful thinking."
sents.cn: 这部分可能由自我欺骗或"一厢情愿"所驱动。

sents.en: The final potential cause is an increase in snacking and eating out over recent decades· both in terms of how often they happen and how much they contribute to our overall energy intake.
sents.cn: 最后一个潜在原因，是近几十年来零食和外食的增多——无论是发生频率，还是它们在我们整体能量摄入中所占的比重。

sents.en: Again, there is evidence that food consumed out of the home is one of the most poorly recorded categories in surveys.
sents.cn: 同样，有证据表明，在家庭之外消费的食物，是调查中记录最差的类别之一。

sents.en: So, what's the message conveyed?
sents.cn: 那么，传达的信息是什么？

sents.en: For statistics, we should invest in more accurate measurement options.
sents.cn: 对统计而言，我们应当投入更精确的测量手段；

sents.en: For policy, we need to focus on options that make it easy for people to eat fewer calories.
sents.cn: 对政策而言，我们需要聚焦于那些让人们轻松减少卡路里摄入的方案。

sents.en: If people do not know how much they are eating, it can be really hard for them to stick to a diet.
sents.cn: 如果人们不知道自己吃了多少，就很难坚持节食。

sents.en: Also, we should be looking for new ways to ensure what people eat wouldn't have much impact on their waistlines.
sents.cn: 此外，我们应寻找新办法，确保人们吃的东西不会对其腰围产生太大影响。

sents.en: If this works, it won't matter if they can't remember what they ate yesterday.
sents.cn: 如果这招奏效，那么即便他们记不起昨天吃了什么，也无所谓了。
